clue.text: Old examination of shepherds

parts.note: old means past, gone by
an oral is a spoken examination

explanation.surface: A historian recalls an ancient test once set for shepherds.
explanation.definitionFit: Pastoral writing and life concern country people tending flocks, so the adjective describes shepherds' world.

clue.text: Not even Patricia went to church last Sunday

parts.note: Pat is short for the name Patricia

indicators.note: last points to the final letter of Sunday

explanation.surface: Patricia attended church only last weekend, it seems.
explanation.definitionFit: Something patchy is uneven, good in some places and poor in others.

clue.text: Man wrong about modus operandi

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the word for wrong goes around the abbreviation

parts.note: a sin is a wrong
MO is the abbreviation for modus operandi, a method of working

explanation.surface: A man has misjudged a criminal's working method.
explanation.definitionFit: Simon is a male first name, so it stands for a man.

clue.text: Steer run away six-footer included, the beast

indicators.note: included means taken inside, so the six-footer goes within the other pieces

parts.note: a steer is a castrated bull, an ox
to elope is to run away to marry
an ant is an insect with six legs, a six-footer

explanation.surface: A bullock bolts, and a giant is caught up with the animal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'six-footer' suggests a tall person but means an insect, with six feet.
explanation.definitionFit: The ox antelope is a large antelope, a wild beast.

clue.text: Large pair of spectacles used for card-game

parts.note: two letter O's look like a pair of glasses

explanation.surface: Big glasses worn for playing cards.
explanation.definitionFit: Loo is an old gambling card game, a game played with a pack.

clue.text: Very nearly everybody had an objection

parts.note: everybody means all
a but is an objection, as in 'no ifs or buts'

explanation.surface: Almost the whole company raised some protest.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is an idiom meaning almost entirely, as in 'it was finished, or nearly so'.

clue.text: Fat landowner from north of the border disheartened

indicators.note: disheartened means losing its heart, so the middle letter is dropped

parts.words: landowner from north of the border
parts.note: a laird is a Scottish landowner, north of the English border

explanation.surface: An overweight Scottish estate owner is feeling low.
explanation.walkthrough: 'disheartened' removes the middle letter I from LAIRD.
explanation.definitionFit: Lard is rendered pig fat used in cooking.

clue.text: Subject on which one is ignorant, motorist cannot see it

definitions.text: Subject on which one is ignorant

explanation.surface: A driver admits a gap in knowledge, and a gap in vision.
explanation.definitionFit: Figuratively an area of ignorance; literally the zone behind a driver that mirrors do not show.

clue.text: Tall plants will not grow beyond it

definitions.text: Tall plants will not grow beyond it

parts.words: Tall plants will not grow beyond it
parts.note: describes the altitude on a mountain above which woodland stops, a limit for timber growth

explanation.definitionFit: The upper limit of forest on a slope, where conditions become too harsh for trees.

clue.text: Reserves ripped map of town in Florida

parts.note: TA is the Territorial Army, Britain's army reserve

indicators.note: a ripped map is torn apart, so its letters are set in a new order

explanation.surface: Army reservists have torn up the map of a Florida town.
explanation.walkthrough: The Territorial Army is Britain's volunteer reserve force, hence 'Reserves'; 'ripped' scrambles the map into MPA.
explanation.definitionFit: Tampa is a city on the Gulf coast of Florida, a place in that state.

clue.text: Despite timidity, beast went a little way by frozen water

parts.note: a cow is a farm beast
RD is the short form of road, a way written small
frozen water is ice

explanation.surface: Though shy, an animal walked a short distance beside an icy pond.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Despite' and 'went' only dress the surface. 'A little way' is a short road, written in its abbreviated form.
explanation.definitionFit: Cowardice is lack of courage, a timid and fearful nature.

clue.text: Dependent on north Dakota entering reassembled coalition

indicators.note: entering means going inside, so the state abbreviation goes within the rearranged letters
reassembled means put together again in a new order

parts.note: ND is the abbreviation for the US state of North Dakota

explanation.surface: A coalition is rebuilt only if North Dakota joins.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dependent' looks like a noun but is the adjective; 'reassembled' gives COITIONAL and 'entering' slips the state in early.
explanation.definitionFit: Conditional means subject to a condition, relying on something else.

clue.text: Decorated press, it's more rust-resistant than steel

parts.note: wrought means worked or ornamented
to iron is to press clothes

explanation.surface: A fancy printing press is claimed to resist corrosion better than steel.
explanation.definitionFit: Wrought iron, low in carbon and fibrous with slag, corrodes more slowly than ordinary steel.

clue.text: New sunhat new? Not new found in seaside resort

indicators.note: new here means made over, so the letters of sunhat are set out afresh
a second 'new' asks for the following letters to be put in a fresh order too

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether a sun hat bought at the coast is new, and is told it is not.
explanation.walkthrough: 'New' turns SUNHAT into HUNSTA; 'new?' turns NOT plus N into NTON. HUNSTANTON is a seaside town on the Norfolk coast of England.
explanation.definitionFit: Hunstanton is a coastal holiday town in Norfolk, a place people visit by the sea.

clue.text: Said Olivia embraced hero

indicators.note: embraced means held within, so the answer sits inside the words Said Olivia

explanation.surface: Olivia is reported to have hugged the man she looked up to.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone adored and admired is a hero to their fans, a figure of worship.

clue.text: These days during breather arranged outside, it is ragged

indicators.note: during means within a span, so the abbreviation sits inside
outside means the rearranged letters wrap round the abbreviation
arranged means put in a new order

parts.note: AD, anno Domini, marks the present era, these days

explanation.surface: A rest break is reorganised outdoors, and it looks shabby.
explanation.walkthrough: 'breather' means a rest, but here it is just letters; 'arranged' gives THREBARE, with 'during' and 'outside' both saying the era sits within.
explanation.definitionFit: Threadbare cloth is worn thin, shabby and tattered.

clue.text: Discussing business — but nothing is ever decided in it

definitions.text: nothing is ever decided in it

explanation.surface: A committee chats about its affairs but never settles anything.
explanation.definitionFit: Literally the phrase means talking about work; as an idiom it names a meeting or body that debates endlessly without action.

clue.text: Amphibian, for example, on short grass to some extent

parts.note: a toad is an amphibian
EG abbreviates exempli gratia, for example

indicators.note: short means cut, so the last letter of reed is lost

parts.note: a reed is a tall grass

explanation.surface: An amphibian, say, sits on cropped lawn to a degree.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is an idiom meaning partly or somewhat.

clue.text: Surprised expression when business comes to nothing

parts.note: CO is the abbreviation for company, a business
O is the round figure zero, nothing

explanation.surface: Someone gasps when their firm collapses into ruin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Coo!' is an informal British exclamation of surprise.
explanation.definitionFit: A mild British exclamation of astonishment, like 'gosh' or 'wow'.

clue.text: Chirps not excitedly to start with in direction of western racecourse

indicators.note: not means without, so a letter is taken out of the word for chirps

parts.note: cheeps are chirps, as from a bird

indicators.note: to start with points to the first letter of excitedly

parts.note: to means towards, in the direction of

explanation.surface: Chirping calmly, a bird heads west to the races.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not' and 'to start with' take E, the first letter of 'excitedly', out of CHEEPS. CHEPSTOW is a horse-racing course in Monmouthshire, Wales.
explanation.definitionFit: Chepstow is a well-known horse-racing venue in south Wales.

clue.text: Leading figure

parts.note: seems to describe a prominent person, but means the numeral that comes first in counting

explanation.definitionFit: The first number in counting leads all the others, so it is the leading digit.

clue.text: Job date

explanation.surface: A diary entry for a job interview.
explanation.definitionFit: A post someone is given is a job; a fixed meeting arranged for a set time is a date.

clue.text: Refer to short publicity announcement

explanation.surface: A brief notice pointing to some product.
explanation.definitionFit: To advert to is a formal way to mention; an advert is a commercial, abbreviated from advertisement.

clue.text: Couple have short letter for homework

parts.note: PR is the standard abbreviation for pair, a couple

indicators.note: short means cut down, so only the opening of the word epistle remains

parts.note: an epistle is a letter

explanation.surface: Two people receive a brief note about school assignments.
explanation.walkthrough: 'short' cuts EPISTLE down to EP. PREP is British school slang for homework, short for preparation.
explanation.definitionFit: Prep is British school slang for work set to be done out of lessons.

clue.text: Brought in Dutch into doctrine that had been reformulated

indicators.note: into means put inside, so the Dutch abbreviation goes within the rearranged letters
something reformulated is recast, so the letters of doctrine are rearranged

explanation.surface: A Dutch idea was smuggled into a creed that had been rewritten.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Brought in' could be read as wordplay, but it is the definition; 'that had been reformulated' gives INTROCED, which 'into' opens up for the Dutch.
explanation.definitionFit: Something introduced has been brought in for the first time, as a new law or product.

clue.text: Inquisitive American leaving rare object

indicators.note: leaving means departing, so the American abbreviation comes out of the word

parts.note: inquisitive means curious
US is the United States, American

explanation.surface: A nosy American leaves behind an unusual item.
explanation.definitionFit: A curio is an unusual collectable item, prized for being uncommon.

clue.text: Flowerbed in the desert?

parts.note: a flower is read as something that flows, a stream, so its bed is a dry desert watercourse

explanation.definitionFit: A wadi is a dry riverbed in desert country that fills only in the rainy season.

clue.text: Sailor man has fashionable waterproof

parts.note: tar is an old word for a sailor
Paul is a man's name
in means fashionable, as in 'the in thing'

explanation.surface: A seaman owns a trendy rain jacket.
explanation.definitionFit: A tarpaulin is a heavy waterproofed canvas sheet, used to keep rain off.

clue.text: I put on pounds when unwell

indicators.note: put on means placed above, so the letter goes on top of the rest in this down entry

parts.note: L is the abbreviation for pound, so LL is pounds

explanation.surface: Someone gains weight when they are sick.
explanation.definitionFit: Ill means sick, in poor health.

clue.text: Come to the same conclusion

parts.note: reads as two people independently reaching one verdict, which is to concur

explanation.definitionFit: To concur is to share an opinion, arriving at a single shared view.

clue.text: Small mostly disgusting beetle

parts.note: wee is Scottish for small

indicators.note: mostly means most but not all, so the last letter of vile is dropped

parts.note: vile means disgusting

explanation.surface: A tiny, nasty little bug.
explanation.definitionFit: A weevil is a small beetle with a long snout that feeds on grain and plants.

clue.text: Bite loaf floating from rescue craft

indicators.note: floating means drifting loose, so the letters of bite loaf move around

explanation.surface: Someone takes a bite of bread drifting from a rescue boat.
explanation.definitionFit: A lifeboat is a vessel launched to save people at sea, a rescue boat.
